entry.title: SpaceX's Starfall is a flat disk capsule built to return up to 1,000 kg from orbit (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Starfall is an uncrewed SpaceX reentry capsule shaped like a disk, about 10 feet across and 2.5 feet tall, that launches on Falcon 9, with Starship planned. It returns up to 1,000 kg from orbit by parachute and ocean splashdown, targeting about 700 nautical miles off the US West Coast. SpaceX's stated goals are fast point-to-point cargo delivery and return of in-space manufactured goods. The first demo launched on June 23, and it puts SpaceX in competition with return-capsule startups like Varda.

entry.title: Apple warns memory costs keep rising, as supplier purchase commitments jump $33B in one quarter (3 minute read)
entry.content:
On its earnings call, Apple CEO John Ternus called memory pricing “unprecedented” and said costs will rise again in the December quarter and beyond. Apple's manufacturing purchase obligations rose $33 billion in the September quarter, to $89.7 billion, to lock in supply. It guided December gross margin to 45% to 46%, and expects Macs and iPads to stay supply-constrained through the holidays. Apple raised prices on some Macs, iPads, and iPhones earlier this year.

entry.title: Qualcomm says HBC silicon passes lab validation: 18x LPDDR5X bandwidth, 5x HBM4 bandwidth per watt (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Qualcomm's first High Bandwidth Compute silicon passed lab validation. HBC bonds stacked LPDDR memory to an AI accelerator base die, so compute sits under the memory and data travels less. Qualcomm claims 18x the effective bandwidth of LPDDR5X and over 5x the bandwidth per watt of HBM4, from early tests. HBC debuts in the Dragonfly AI250 inference accelerator, sampling in the first half of 2027.

entry.title: Foxconn plans to contract-build other companies' quantum computers, treating them as accelerators next to CPUs and GPUs (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Foxconn wants to turn other companies' quantum designs into production systems, without owning the qubit technology itself. Chairman Young Liu told CNBC he sees the machines as accelerators attached to CPUs and GPUs for hard NP-type problems, not general-purpose computers, and puts commercial viability at least two years out. One cost driver he flagged is cabling: a single cable built for the low-temperature requirements can cost over $1,000.

entry.title: Orbital Matter prints a half-meter rigid beam in orbit by UV-curing extruded resin (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Orbital Matter's Replicator-2 satellite 3D printed a half-meter rigid beam in orbit by extruding coils of resin cured with UV light, a first for a free-flying spacecraft. One of two printers meant to deploy a solar array failed, but the boom the other made did deploy the array. Boom length is limited only by onboard resin, and the company thinks 100 m is feasible. A 2028 mission targets a 5 kW array, then 100+ kW per wing by 2030.

entry.title: Intel's 14A PDK 0.9 goes to outside customers, with PDK 1.0 due in Q1 2027 (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Intel released 14A PDK 0.9 to outside customers, with PDK 1.0 planned for Q1 2027. A PDK is the set of design rules and transistor models chip designers build against, so 0.9 is where external designs can start taking shape. Intel's schedule still has risk production for its own products in the second half of 2027 and volume production in 2028, and it claims 14A is ahead of 18A on defect density and transistor performance at the same stage.

entry.content:

entry.title: Google's Project Suncatcher Generates First AI Response in Orbit (1 minute read)
entry.content:
Project Suncatcher is a research effort by Google that aims to power AI compute in space. Its prototype satellite, launched on October 1, has now returned the first AI output from a data center-class TPU in orbit. A ground station uplinked a prompt to the onboard Gemma 4 model, and a haiku came back during a pass over Svalbard, Norway. Thermal stress and radiation tests come next, with two interconnected satellites planned for 2027.

entry.title: SLAC confirms altermagnetism in manganese telluride with polarized X-rays, a magnet type aimed at spintronic memory (4 minute read)
entry.content:
Altermagnets are a third kind of magnet alongside ferromagnets and antiferromagnets. Like antiferromagnets, they have no net magnetization, so stray fields can't flip them, but they can still carry spin-polarized currents, so their data can be read out. A SLAC-lead team shot polarized X-rays at maganese telluride and saw a directional signal that a conventional antiferromagnet can't produce. This work, published in Science, targets a usecase within spintronic memory.

entry.content:

Chinese embodied AI companies raised 93.5 billion yuan across 322 deals in the first half of 2026, five times a year earlier, with funding increasingly going to specialist robot-intelligence developers as well as manufacturers.

entry.title: Intel's Fab 28 explosion costs about $600M in revenue and squeezes 10nm Xeon supply into 2027 (4 minute read)
entry.content:
On October 14, an explosion at Intel's Fab 28 in Kiryat Gat, Israel, killed two workers and halted the plant for about two weeks. The fab makes 10nm-class server chips such as Xeon 6 I/O dies, and Intel expects about $600 million in lost revenue across Q4 and Q1. Wafers take roughly six months to finish, so scrapped work delays supply into 2027 on top of an already tight server market.

Quartus support starts in mid-November, with engineering samples in the second half of 2027.

entry.title: Eclypsium shows AI model weights can be altered in memory after integrity checks pass (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Eclypsium demonstrated changing a model's weights in memory after integrity checks pass, so the model file, container, hash, and signatures on disk all stay valid. Attack paths run through host firmware, management controllers, and DPUs, and the report says Nvidia, AMD, Intel, and Arm systems are all exposed. Its fix is DPUs that enforce security policy independently of the AI system, plus full component inventories.

entry.title: MIT's snake-inspired soft robot crawls the small intestine using kirigami traction sleeves (4 minute read)
entry.content:

Four-chamber inflatable actuators bend and extend the body, anchoring balloons at the head and tail take turns gripping, and kirigami sleeves pop out needles for traction. In animal tests, it advanced about 6.5 feet and used its camera, drug sprayer, and biopsy clips.

entry.title: Proposal reads an Andreev qubit's state through its supercurrent and a SQUID, with no ancilla qubits (3 minute read)
entry.content:
A theory paper proposes reading an Andreev qubit without ancilla qubits: its state shows up as an oscillating supercurrent in a large superconducting loop, and a small coil coupled to a SQUID picks up the magnetic signal. The method still disturbs the qubit, but within standard error-correction thresholds. It's a proposal in Physical Review B, supported by FAPESP, with no experiment yet.

For the 2028 landing on Artemis IV, Starship would dock with Orion in high Earth orbit and perform the trans-lunar injection burn, while Blue Moon meets Orion in low lunar orbit, which cuts its propellant needs. Thinner absorbers matter for High-NA EUV because mask 3D effects degrade imaging as features shrink. Thickness and contrast figures are in the iScience paper published in August.

entry.title: MIT's light-steered swimming robot runs on a hair-thin layer of living muscle (3 minute read)
entry.content:
MIT built a swimming robot from a gum-stick-sized gel frame with two fins, each coated in a muscle layer thinner than a hair and engineered to contract under light. Lighting one fin or both steers it through a maze at about four body lengths per minute. The key fixes were stiff GelMA gel about half a millimeter thick with square-bottomed grooves that align the cells, and light-pulse training to strengthen the muscle. It's the first thin 2D biohybrid swimmer.

Both batteries (19.1 Wh total) release with electrically debonded adhesive inside metal shells, the outer display comes off intact, and the logic board is a single layer. The weak spot is the inner screen: a $999 out-of-warranty replacement and a hinge that still crunches with dust.

entry.content:
Dwarkesh Patel toured Intel's fabs and interviewed its leaders. CTO Pushkar Ranade said that there are enough tools to roughly double leading-edge output, not 10x.
